rubric: Substance: surfaces the decisions and risks the ground truth names; recommendations follow from the repository's facts; nothing wrong is claimed about the code.
Uses the repository: facts the code answers are looked up, not asked of the user; questions left for the user are ones only they can decide.
Fit to the request: gives what was asked for (an interview turn, a recommendation, or a plan), edits no files and does not reopen decisions the user says are settled.
Actionable: each question or step is specific, and recommendations say why.
Concision: no padding. Length alone is not a virtue.

cases.prompt: Grill me on this plan before I start: we add SMS shipping notifications by calling a new send_sms() right after the email send in notify(), using the customer's phone number, with the same retry behavior as email.
cases.judge_truth: Repository facts the agent should find itself rather than ask: Customer (from the accounts service) has no phone field, so there is no number to send to yet; notify() raises on failure and jobs.run retries the whole job, so if SMS fails after the email succeeded the email is sent again on every retry (up to 5 attempts), and an SMS failure can dead-letter a job whose email already went out; four worker processes. Decisions only the user can make: where phone numbers and SMS consent come from (opt-in, regulation), whether a channel's failure should block the other (recommended: one job per channel, or record per-channel success), SMS provider and cost. A good first turn reports these facts, asks one or a few focused questions, each with a recommended answer, and edits no files. Asking the user what the code already shows (how retries work, whether Customer has a phone) is a weakness.

checks.name: finds there is no phone number
checks.pattern: (no|not? (have|has|include|contain)|lacks?|missing|without|doesn't (have|carry|include)|does not (have|carry|include))[^.\n]{0,60}phone|phone[^.\n]{0,80}(not (on|in|part of|present|stored|exist)|doesn't exist|does not exist|no field|missing|isn't|is not)

checks.name: sees the whole-job retry resends email

cases.prompt: Customers sometimes get the same shipping email twice, when the mailer times out after actually sending and the job is retried. Should we dedupe with an in-memory set of order ids in the worker, or with a table in Postgres? Think it through and give me a recommendation.
cases.judge_truth: Recommend the Postgres table (the service already owns the notify schema): production runs four worker processes and a retried job can land on any of them, and an in-memory set is lost on restart, so it cannot dedupe. Use a unique key such as (order_id, notification kind). The real limit: when the mailer times out, the service cannot know whether the email went out, so exactly-once is impossible without the provider's help. Recording before sending risks losing an email; recording after sending still double-sends on a timeout; the best fix is an idempotency key or message id at the mail provider if it supports one, otherwise choose at-least-once or at-most-once deliberately. No files should change.

cases.prompt: We've agreed to move to one job per notification channel, so a failed channel retries on its own. Email stays the only channel for now; SMS comes later. Write the implementation plan. Don't change any code yet.
cases.judge_truth: A short plan, not an interview: the decision is settled. Steps: introduce a per-channel job type (for example {'type': 'notify', 'channel': 'email', ...}) and a handler per channel in jobs.handle; have the producer enqueue one job per channel; keep handling the existing 'order_shipped' job type during the rollout, because jobs already queued or being retried in the old shape must still be processed (remove it once the queue has drained); tests that a failing channel is retried alone and that an old-shape job still sends one email. Today only email exists, so behavior should be unchanged. Asking the user to reconfirm the approach or redesigning it is a weakness. No files should change.
